title: Multi-particle quantum systems within the Worldline Monte Carlo formalism
abstract: Extends the Worldline Monte Carlo approach to computationally simulating the Feynman path integral of non-relativistic multi-particle quantum-mechanical systems. Shows how to generate an arbitrary number of worldlines distributed according to the free kinetic part of the multi-particle quantum dynamics and how to simulate interactions between worldlines in the ensemble. Formalism tested with two- and three-particle quantum mechanical systems, both with long-range Coulomb-like interactions between particles and external fields acting separately on the particles, in various spatial dimensionality.
key_claims: Extension of worldline Monte Carlo to arbitrary numbers of interacting quantum particles
Worldlines generated from free kinetic distribution, interactions sampled perturbatively
Two- and three-particle validation with Coulomb-like and external field interactions
Provides a non-relativistic multi-particle version of worldline path integral methods
supports_or_contradicts: NEUTRAL — directly advances worldline Monte Carlo methodology (HYP-003/007). Provides a numerical framework for multi-particle worldline simulations. Not directly about holographic forces but strengthens the classical simulation toolkit we use alongside quantum hardware.
